title: POC Weekly Caching Sync - BrightCart POC
header:
Date: 2026-07-14 | Time: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood CSM), Liam Chen (BrightCart Head of ML), Sofia Ramirez (BrightCart Platform Eng), Ethan Brooks (BrightCart Product), Nina Patel (BrightCart SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on caching results and prompt reuse strategy. Reviewed current KV/prefix cache hit rates, root causes for misses, and tuning approaches (key canonicalization, TTL, cache warming). Agreed on short-term experiments to improve hit rates and a timeline for validation benchmarks next week. Action items assigned for changes to prompt templating, cache key rules, and an expanded benchmark run on dedicated capacity.
topics: Current KV cache hit rates and distribution
Instrumentation and metrics to track (per-route hit rate, latency)
action_items: Priya: Share updated cache-keying README and example regexes by 2026-07-16
Liam: Provide 3 representative prompt families and expected invariants by 2026-07-16
Sofia: Deploy TTL change to staging (reduce to 10m for low-value prompts) and report metrics by 2026-07-20
Jordan: Spin up a dedicated canary with 2x capacity for 24h benchmark and share cost estimate by 2026-07-17
Miguel: Send security/SOC2 checklist and link to VPC docs to Nina by 2026-07-15
next_steps: Implement prompt canonicalization heuristics and re-run benchmark with 1M requests
Tune prefix cache key extraction and add fallthrough rules for rarely seen tokens
Run 24h canary on dedicated nodes to validate latency and hit-rate improvements
Share benchmark spreadsheet and updated dashboard link with BrightCart team
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: ok hey everyone thanks for joining the weekly caching sync, we'll go 42 minutes ish, agenda quick review of last weeks changes and the hit rate numbers, then tuning and action items
[00:18] Liam Chen: yeah thanks Jordan, quick note we ran the 100k request pass over staging yesterday, saw some uplift but still a bunch of misses in the cart recovery flow
[00:34] Priya Nair: got it liam can you share the specific prompt samples? i saw overall KV hit~62% but prefix-only hits were down at 48% for conversational paths
[00:50] Liam Chen: yes i'll attach later but it's mainly templates where user metadata gets injected — e.g. items list, promo codes, user history — little permutations cause new keys
[01:05] Sofia Ramirez: and on our side we're worried about TTLs, currently it's 1 hour default, which seems long for ephemeral carts causing stale entries but also we lose some reuse because of tiny token differences
[01:22] Priya Nair: two quick observations from Redwood SE side: 1) canonicalizing prompt inputs before keying increases prefix reuse a lot (strip whitespace, normalize punctuation, collapse list order for product lists where order doesn't matter), 2) employ hashed bucket keys for large lists to avoid huge key space
[01:40] Ethan Brooks: curious about how much effort canonicalization is — will it require changes to product side?
[01:47] Priya Nair: minimal, usually a small shim in the prompt builder or on the server side that normalizes strings; we can provide examples and regex rules
[02:05] Jordan Hayes: log numbers we have: KV cache overall hit 62% (as priya said), prefix cache hit 48%, tail latency for misses increased by ~30ms, token cost per request down 12% when hit occurs — those are day 2 numbers post-change
[02:25] Liam Chen: ok that matches our spreadsheet, but a lot of misses are from user-specific metadata and promo codes that vary by region
[02:33] Nina Patel: security question — if we canonicalize do we strip PII? We need to ensure no customer-identifiable fields are part of keys, otherwise encryption/KMS needs to be considered
[02:45] Miguel Santos: good call, we'll ensure canonicalization includes PII redaction and use non-reversible hashing for any identifiers used in keys; i'll follow up with a security checklist link
[03:00] Priya Nair: on TTL tuning, for low value prompts 10 minutes gives most of the reuse without much staleness; for conversation state maybe longer, we can make tiered TTLs per route
[03:18] Sofia Ramirez: can we do tiered TTLs now in staging? we can try 10m low, 30m mid, 2h for session summaries
[03:27] Priya Nair: yes that's simple configuration change on our end — we can push to staging this week
[03:35] Jordan Hayes: regarding cache warming — if you know heavy-upfront flows (holiday promo blast etc) we can pre-warm by seeding keys via a warm job, also batching windows can be tuned to improve throughput without affecting latency too much
[03:50] Ethan Brooks: pre-warm sounds great for the promo window, how expensive is it?
[03:55] Priya Nair: cost depends on number of unique keys seeded; we can estimate from logs — usually cheap compared to missed LLM tokens at scale
[04:05] Liam Chen: what's the expected improvement if we canonicalize plus TTL changes? a target would be nice
[04:12] Priya Nair: conservative estimate from similar customers: raise prefix hit from 48% -> ~72-78% with canonicalization + key bucketization; overall KV hit could move 62% -> ~80% if we combine with TTL tiering and warming
[04:28] Jordan Hayes: ok that's encouraging, let's plan a benchmark: 1M requests rerun with canonicalization + TTL + warming, run on dedicated canary for 24h, compare hit rates and costs
[04:40] Sofia Ramirez: do we need dedicated nodes for that? staging capacity might not reflect production behavior
[04:46] Jordan Hayes: yes dedicated canary recommended to mirror production; i'll provide cost and an approval ticket, we can run 24h and then scale back
[04:55] Miguel Santos: security/ops -- i'll send VPC and SOC2 docs to Nina and include checklist items about PII in cache keys
[05:05] Nina Patel: thanks miguel, also we'll want RBAC controls on who can change cache-key rules in prod
[05:12] Priya Nair: logging: we suggest adding per-route hit-rate dashboards and a histogram of key frequency; small change to instrumentation but big visibility payoff
[05:25] Jordan Hayes: ok i will share a dashboard link and the benchmark spreadsheet post-call
[05:30] Liam Chen: timeline wise, we'll: provide prompt families by EOD Thursday, staging TTL change by next Monday, and expect canary cost estimate by Friday
[05:42] Jordan Hayes: recap action items and owners — priya will share cache-keying README, lijam? (small stutter) liam will send prompts, sasha? (mislabel) sofia will do TTL deploy, miguel will send security links, jordan will spin up canary estimate and share dashboard
[06:05] Ethan Brooks: small question about prompt reuse: for cart items list can we canonicalize by sorting SKUs? if order doesn't matter that would help a lot
[06:14] Priya Nair: yes canonical sorting is a recommended pattern, we can provide helper code snippet for that
[06:22] Liam Chen: we'll also audit our front end templating to avoid injecting session-specific IDs into prompts
[06:30] Jordan Hayes: perfect, any blockers?
[06:33] Nina Patel: no blockers, just need the SOC2 link and RBAC proposal
[06:36] Miguel Santos: i'll attach both after the call
[06:40] Jordan Hayes: great thanks everyone we'll sync same time next week and aim to have the 1M benchmark results in the following weekly call
[06:48] (crosstalk) Sofia Ramirez: thanks all
[06:50] Jordan Hayes: bye everyone
